title: Price-Protection Refunds: The Days-Since-Completion Allowance
content:
# Price-protection refunds: the days-since-completion allowance

Refund desk rule, Cartwise Grocery Orders.

**Rule.** The price-protection standing allowance is added to the price-protection refund after the refund is rounded to the cent. When at least 2 calendar days have passed from the date of the order's completion to today and no price-protection refund stands on the order yet, the allowance is 1.00. When exactly 1 calendar day has passed and none stands yet, it is 0.50. Otherwise there is none. The refund with the allowance never exceeds the line's billed charge.

**Counting the days.** The date part of the order's completion time is day 0; each following calendar date adds one day, regardless of the hour.

**Reading the order.** "A price-protection refund stands on the order" means an item refund entry with the reason substitution price protection is already among the order's entries.

| Days since completion | Price-protection refund already on the order | Allowance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 or more | none | 1.00 |
| exactly 1 | none | 0.50 |
| 0 | none | none |
| any | one already stands | none |

Hypothetical figures: a rounded refund of 0.60 with 5 days since completion and none yet on the order becomes 1.60, which is within a line charge of 7.80. On a line charged 1.10, the same 1.60 is held at 1.10.
